title: Build a goal to completion: expansion runs, next-node proposals, parallel seats
description:
Filed by architect-16a01670 from parent task-e7a3d643bde34da7b27495dbda745739 (epic breakdown, human-directed 2026-09-04).

PRODUCT GAP (README, re-measured 2026-09-04): 'an initial plan seals one node, so a goal is built one node at a time and growth goes through a successor goal.' Measured: core finalize refuses multi-node INITIAL runs (`packages/core/src/planning/planning-run-submission.ts` MULTI_NODE_EXECUTION_UNSUPPORTED, design 396/1322 - a FENCE, keep it); the compiler mirrors it (`apps/daemon/src/planning/compile-dispatcher.ts:192-197` SUBMIT_DECOMPOSITION_MULTI_NODE_INITIAL). Core already models `PlanningRunKind = INITIAL|REVISION|EXPANSION` with EXPANSION_PLANNING holds and sealed expansion proposals (`packages/core/src/planning/planning-command-contract.ts:11,138-202`, planning-event-contract.ts:49-115), and DONE rows landed the expansion prerequisites (task-671cdd10 'select the durable released attempt for an expansion parent', task-e62e3828 'current expansion safe-release evidence') - but NO expansion kind is published on the daemon vocabulary (`grep -c request_expansion apps/daemon/src/daemon-command-vocabulary.ts` = 0). Growth today = REPLAN successor goal (apps/control-room/src/v2/approvals/replan-successor-port.ts).

FEATURE: after a node is accepted and landed (COMMITTED `moe-landing-receipt/1`), the daemon opens an EXPANSION planning run on the SAME goal; the wrapper staffs a planning seat whose mission carries the approved contract plus the coverage read's UNCOVERED criteria (`POST /documents/coverage/read`); the seat submits the next node(s) through the MCP `planning.submit_decomposition` path extended for EXPANSION (multi-node is allowed there by core design; HARD edges between dependent nodes); the human approves the expansion in the browser (plan-approval card reused, one decision); the wrapper staffs EVERY READY unclaimed node - independent nodes in parallel, bounded by a durable per-project seat limit (default 2) shown on Seats; the goal is 'ready to close' only when every approved criterion is covered. No successor goal for growth (REPLAN stays for exhausted reviews).

ALSO FIX (measured 2026-09-04 on UnAI goal-c9d9850b, memory real-seat-cannot-release-its-claim-2026-09-04): `work_get_context` ignores its `workItemId` (60 KB global dump; claimAggregateVersion unreachable when the harness truncates) and `EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT` carries no observed version, so a real seat cannot `work_release` and its claim lapses at the 30-min TTL. This row makes work_get_context honour workItemId (or returns claimAggregateVersion in the work_claim receipt) and puts `observedVersion` in the refusal details - a multi-node goal cannot be staffed twice without it.

UI: the board (PR #23, apps/control-room/src/v2/board/) shows every node across its six columns; the goal status strip reads 'N of M criteria covered - expansion proposed / awaiting your approval / building'; Needs-you gets 'Approve expansion' (offer-wire pattern); Seats shows the concurrency limit.

DESIGN CONSTRAINT: never relax the INITIAL one-node fence; route growth through EXPANSION (memory initial-run-seals-one-node-by-core-design).
definitionOfDone: Daemon publishes the expansion kinds (architect names them, e.g. `graph.request_expansion` plus the EXPANSION arm of planning.submit_decomposition) with the full roster backfill (vocabulary, registry ROWS + REGISTRATION_ORDER + size pins, families, v2 registry, MCP allowlist/exclusions, generated client + every digest mirror); roster tests assert set-equality in both directions.

e2e over a REAL daemon with a scripted seat double on the real MCP wire: node 1 lands -> expansion run opened -> 2 nodes proposed -> approved in the browser -> both staffed -> delivered, verified, landed on the SAME goal; the goal reaches ready-to-close only at 100% criteria coverage; assert node count = 3 and every criterion VERIFIED on the coverage read.

Wrapper test: two independent READY nodes produce two SPAWNED seats before either exits; a HARD-dependent node is not staffed until its parent is DONE; the durable per-project limit (default 2) is honoured and disclosed on /sessions/read.

`work_get_context {workItemId}` returns that item's claim only (claimAggregateVersion present, response under 8 KB for one item) and `EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT` details carry `observedVersion`; a seat-double test releases its claim on the first try; the refusal test asserts code + layer + observedVersion.
Core fence untouched: the MULTI_NODE_EXECUTION_UNSUPPORTED arm still refuses a 2-node INITIAL run, and mutating compile-dispatcher.ts to allow it turns that test red (drill recorded in a step note).

Live drive on UnAI (goal-c9d9850b or a fresh goal): a second node proposed, approved and landed on the same goal - transcript + landing shas in a row comment; README 'one node at a time' sentence rewritten to the measured truth.
Gates quoted with their count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm test:e2e`.

If the plan exceeds the daemon's thresholds (12 steps / 10 files), the planning architect SPIDR-splits into children under THIS row (parentTaskId); children may depend on each other, never on a sibling feature row.

FEATURES ONLY (human DoD 2026-09-04): no security-boundary or policy work in this row. The verifier stays the documented trusted-workspace v0.1 limitation; signing, hermetic verification and freeze manifests are out of scope.

HUMAN GATES ARE HUMAN-ONLY: every approve/decide kind this row adds is operator-only, listed in HUMAN_ONLY_STEPS and MCP-excluded; every refusal carries a stable code asserted by a test (global rail 1); roster tests are bidirectional set-equality (global rail 9). A new daemon read/command follows the 8-touchpoint + .js bridge pattern (memory ui-connect-everything-built-2026-09-02).

PROVE IT LIVE: besides an offline e2e over a REAL daemon (no fixtures), completion records a live drive on the lane (UnAI at D:/projexts/UnAI or a fresh project): transcript, store path and sha in a row comment (keep each comment under 4500 chars). Never restart the wrapper to unstick a seat (claim TTL 30 min, memory real-seat-cannot-release-its-claim-2026-09-04).

implementationPlan.note:
ADVERSARIAL PASS OVER THE COMPOSED FEATURE (integration level, across all six diffs). Read-only; every claim measured at HEAD.

(a) DOES THE DEPENDENCY GATE AGREE WITH THE BOARD? YES — byte-for-byte the same derivation, in both files: `compiled-node-source.ts:134` `dependsOn: edges.filter((edge) => edge.consumerNodeKey === definition.nodeKey).map((edge) => edge.producerNodeKey)` (feeds `NodeSpec.dependsOn` at :186, which `affordance-read.ts:442` consumes) and `runs-read.ts:98-104` — identical expression, and the source carries a comment naming runs-read as the reason. Both also filter to `executionBearing` nodes off `graph.content.snapshot.nodes`. ONE DIVERGENCE, benign but worth recording: compiled-node-source DEDUPES a node key that appears in more than one activated graph (`listed` set at :121-126, first graph wins), while runs-read keeps both rows and instead marks them via `sharedKeysOf()` (:116-120). So with two activated plans carrying the same nodeKey the BOARD can show two cards where the SURFACE staffs one. Build ORDER cannot disagree (same edges, same filter); only cardinality can. Not a defect of this epic — the surface's choice is the safe one (never staff a key twice).

(b) CAN A dependsOn CYCLE REACH THE SURFACE? YES — real gap, filed as comment-982b4569951b42ab9da84c3fafcbe84c on this row rather than a new row (rail 21). Summary: `compiled-authority-bodies.ts:62-75` refuses unknown ref, self-ref and completion-node dependency (`COMPILED_PLAN_MALFORMED`) plus unbound criterion and node budget, but nothing walks the edge set (0 hits for acyclic/cycle/topo/visit/seen in the file). (c) SEAT LIMIT 1, 3-NODE GRAPH — DOES ANYTHING STARVE? NO. `agent-wrapper.ts:352` breaks the loop at `staffing.activeCount() >= config.maxAgents` BEFORE the claim check, so a limit of 1 staffs exactly one node per pass; the pass repeats, and when the seat exits and its node is accepted it leaves READY, so the next node is staffed on the following pass — the graph finishes serially. Three specific starvation traps checked and absent: (i) the attempts counter is incremented only after `staff()` returns and only for non-GATE_REFUSAL outcomes (:365), so a node that is merely limit-deferred never burns an attempt toward `STAFFING_ATTEMPTS_EXHAUSTED`; (ii) `attempts` entries are dropped for anything no longer READY (:341-343), so leaving and re-entering READY re-arms; (iii) `ordered` sorts node.deliver (rank 0) ahead of everything and goal.close (rank 2) last, so a scarce seat can never be consumed by the closure step ahead of unbuilt nodes.

NO — and the premise that it is a NEW member is wrong at HEAD. `readonly observedVersion: number` sits on `CommandDecisionRecordBase` (`packages/store/src/store-contracts.ts:110`) and `git log -S "readonly observedVersion: number;" -- packages/store/src/store-contracts.ts` names ONE commit, **f292887f "feat: add scoped command decision ledger" (2026-08-06)** — it predates this epic by a month and already had consumers (`activation-attempt-reader.ts:115`, `human-approval-authority-reader.ts:62`). Within one wrapper process, NO: passes are serialized by the `pending` promise chain (`agent-wrapper.ts:377-383`, comment "Serialize passes, not child lifetimes: overlapping surface snapshots could double-staff or overshoot maxAgents") and `staffing.has(workItemId)` (:356) rejects an item already in flight.
